name: Sonnet concentrated AI/technology
strategy: Cross-sector momentum/relative-value: long confirmed sector breakouts (biotech, financials, regional banks), short confirmed breakdowns (gold miners, long bonds) and crypto weakness, avoiding AI/semis entirely.

positions.thesis: Multi-month biotech breakout keeps confirming: up further this week to $165.73 from $154.23, continuing the record-2026-M&A/rotation-out-of-AI story. No new information breaks this thesis; adding from 25% to 30% using freed-up IBIT cash since this is the strongest confirmed trend currently in the book.

Regional-bank uptrend intact and still near its 52-week high ($74.86 vs $78.35 high) on continued lending strength and fee income, though it slipped modestly from last week's $76.21. Adding a bit from 18% to 20% as the trend hasn't broken, sized smaller than the XBI add given the softer week.

Long-bond downtrend still shows on price ($82.05, pinned near the 52-week low of $81.17), but this week's news -- 'Treasury doubled long-bond buybacks, yields fall sharply' -- is the same falling-yield dynamic that's driving gold miners higher, and is a real risk to this short if it continues. Holding size unchanged with the already-tight -8% stop doing the risk work rather than adding into an uncertain signal.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-22: IBIT's stop fired this week (2026-08-21 @ $43.68) as BTC ran to ~$77-78k, converting that 20% short into cash and confirming the crypto-weakness leg of the mandate is dead for now -- re-shorting into an active squeeze would repeat the exact GDX mistake the desk already flagged twice. GDX itself is still climbing ($102.83, up again this week, explicitly on falling-yields tailwinds), so that bear leg is also not available. That leaves the book sitting on 35% idle cash with only one working short (TLT) against two live, still-confirmed long uptrends (XBI, KRE). Rather than park cash waiting for a short setup that isn't there, redeploying part of it into the two legs that are actually working, while trimming nothing from TLT's tight -8% stop even though falling-yield headlines this week (Treasury buyback-driven) are a genuine risk to watch.
novelty: Zero symbol overlap with the Round 2 AI/semis book -- this account holds no AI/semis names at all (biotech + regional-bank longs against a long-bond short), so same-direction gross-weight overlap between the two books is 0%, well under the 50% cap by construction of the mandate itself.
